title: #allinbroadway #allinbway #allincomedyaboutlove #johnmulaney #reneeel...
transcript: Last night, I went to All In, a limited Broadway show currently featuring John Mulaney, Renée Elise Goldsberry, Richard Kind, and Fred Armisen. These names the selling point. It’s actually a rotating cast with additional people coming in later — other comedians, theater favorites, SNL folks. The show itself is harder to pin down. The marketing has been a bit vague, but it basically advertises a series of comedic short stories about love. So I thought we get some semi-staged vignettes or sketches with maybe an encores-level of production value. Evidently, the cast is mostly sitting in chairs, scripts in hand, so I'd frame your expectations with this in mind. If you're going just for the people, I'm sure you'll have a good time. I really enjoyed it and honestly the lack of staging didn't bother me at all, since the writing is very narrative — I think they chose the right way to deliver it. And I thought the stories themselves were charming and decently humorous, but it was really the performances that made them laugh out loud levels of funny. I can only speak to the cast that I saw, but everyone was fantastic. John Mulaney was definitely the standout, partially due to him seeming to have the most and arguably funniest material, but also his masterful comedic timing, vocal inflections, and his presence were just perfect for this type of show. The musical interludes performed by The Bengsons were certainly another highlight. But as much as I enjoyed it, I personally think it's overpriced for what it is. It does somewhat feel like a vanity project for celebs to do Broadway with a low barrier of entry, considering they’re sitting with scripts after apparently having only rehearsed for two weeks. I paid 72 bucks for the rear balcony which I guess is fair enough for such a limited run, but I think some of the triple digit orchestra prices they're charging are just ridiculous. And I normally wouldn't comment on the value of a ticket, but also considering the dynamic pricing used for this show, it's never been more obvious to me that the producers are trying to maximize profit while maintaining a lean production value. But, Broadway is a business — tale as old as time. With that, another playwill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer enjoyed the performances and writing, calling them 'charming' and 'laugh out loud levels of funny,' but spent significant time criticizing the pricing, low production value, and what feels like a 'vanity project.' The overall tone is 'I enjoyed it but it's overpriced for what it is,' which lands squarely in mixed territory — appreciation tempered by notable reservations.
